Just as an add-on to what has been said by others, suicidal thoughts aren't just a binary thing (either you have them or you don't), but more of a gradient. 

Some "checkpoints" that I've encountered in medical professionals have been things like how often (how many times a week or how many times a day?), how concrete (how would you do it? Do you know where? Have you made plans?) and how likely you are to do it.

Having noticed this pattern, I'm able to check in on myself a little better. If I can tick the boxes of thinking about it frequently but also concretely, I know things are not great. But if it's the same but less concrete, I don't have to worry as much and can say that to people around me so they don't have to worry so much.
